questions.text:
Consider the following problems. L(G) denotes the language generated by a grammar G. L(M) denotes the language accepted by a machine M.

(I) For an unrestricted grammar G and a string w, whether w[latex]\in [/latex]L(G)
(II) Given a Turing machine M, whether L(M) is regular
(III) Given two grammars G1 and G2, whether L(G1) = L(G2)
(IV) Given an NFA N, whether there is a deterministic PDA P such that N and P accept the same language.

Which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: membership for unrestricted grammars = TM acceptance [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- II: is L(M) regular (Rice) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- III: equivalence of two grammars (even CFGs) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- IV: an NFA's language is regular, and every regular language has a DPDA [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] the answer is always yes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decidable.

Answer: Only I, II and III are undecidable

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Only I and II are undecidable
Only III is undecidable
Only II and IV are undecidable
Only I, II and III are undecidable

questions.text:
A lexical analyzer uses the following patterns to recognize three tokens [latex]T_{1}, T_{2}, \; and \; T_{3} [/latex] over the alphabet {a,b,c}.

[latex]T_{1}:a?(b|c)^* a [/latex]
[latex]T_{2}:b?(a|c)^* b [/latex]
[latex] T_{3}:c?(b|a)^* c[/latex]

Note that 'x?' means 0 or 1 occurrence of the symbol x. Note also that the analyzer outputs the token that matches the longest possible prefix.

If the string bbaacabc is processed by the analyzer, which one of the following is the sequence of tokens it outputs?
questions.solution:
Longest-prefix matching on bbaacabc:
- T1 matches "bba", T2 matches "bb", but T3 = c?(b|a)*c matches "bbaac" (longest) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
- Remaining "abc": T3 matches "abc" [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3

Answer: T3T3

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: [latex]T_{1}T_{2}T_{3}[/latex]
[latex]T_{1}T_{1}T_{3}[/latex]
[latex]T_{2}T_{1}T_{3}[/latex]
[latex]T_{3}T_{3}[/latex]

questions.text:
C onsider the following parse tree for the expression a#b$c$d#e#f, involving two binary operators $ and #.

Which one of the following is correct for the given parse tree?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- $ appears deeper in the tree than #, so it is applied first [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] $ has higher precedence.
- b $ c $ d is grouped as (b $ c) $ d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] $ is left associative.
- a # ([latex]\ldots[/latex] # (e # f)) groups to the right [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] # is right associative.

Answer: $ has higher precedence and is left associative; # is right associative

# has higher precedence and is left associative; [latex]\$[/latex] is right associative
[latex]\$[/latex] has higher precedence and is left associative; # is left associative
# has higher precedence and is right associative; [latex]\$[/latex] is left associative

questions.text:
In a system, there are three types of resources: E, F and G. Four processes [latex]P_0,P_1,P_2 \; and \; P_3[/latex] execute concurrently. At the outset, the processes have declared their maximum resource requirements using a matrix named Max as given below. For example, Max[[latex]P_2[/latex],F] is the maximum number of instances of F that [latex]P_2[/latex] would require. The number of instances of the resources allocated to the various processes at any given state is given by a matrix named Allocation.
Consider a state of the system with the Allocation matrix as shown below, and in which 3 instances of E and 3 instances of F are the only resources available.

From the perspective of deadlock avoidance, which one of the following is true?
questions.solution:
Need = Max [latex]-[/latex] Allocation: P0 (3,3,0), P1 (1,0,2), P2 (0,3,0), P3 (3,4,1). Available (3,3,0).
- P0 can finish [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] available (4,3,1)
- P2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (5,3,4)
- P1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (6,4,6)
- P3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (8,4,6)

Safe sequence P0, P2, P1, P3 exists.

Answer: The system is in safe state

options: The system is in safe state.
The system is not in safe state, but would be safe if one more instance of E were available
The system is not in safe state, but would be safe if one more instance of F were available

questions.text:
Consider the following solution to the producer-consumer synchronization problem. The shared buffer size is N. Three semaphores empty, full and mutex are defined with respective initial values of 0, N and 1. Semaphore empty denotes the number of available slots in the buffer, for the consumer to read from. Semaphore full denotes the number of available slots in the buffer, for the producer to write to. The placeholder variables, denoted by P, Q, R, and S, in the code below can be assigned either empty or full. The valid semaphore operations are: wait() and signal().

Which one of the following assignments to P, Q, R and S will yield the correct solution?
questions.solution:
Here "full" counts free slots (starts at N) and "empty" counts filled slots (starts at 0).
- Producer: wait for a free slot (P = full), add, then signal a filled slot (Q = empty).
- Consumer: wait for a filled slot (R = empty), remove, then signal a free slot (S = full).

Answer: P: full, Q: empty, R: empty, S: full

options: P: full, Q: full, R: empty, S: empty
P: empty, Q: empty, R: full, S: full
P: full, Q: empty, R: empty, S: full
P: empty, Q: full, R: full, S: empty
